stem: Alkanes constitute a homologous series of straight chain saturated hydrocarbons. Write down the structural formulae of the first five homologues of this series. Write their molecular formulae and deduce the general formula of such homologous series.
solution:
The first five homologues are generated by adding one \(\mathrm{-CH_2-}\) at a time, starting with the first homologue \(\mathrm{CH_4}\).

\(\mathrm{CH_4}\) (1st homologue) \(\xrightarrow{\text{add } \mathrm{-CH_2-}}\) \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_3}\) (2nd homologue) \(\xrightarrow{\text{add } \mathrm{-CH_2-}}\) \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_3}\) (3rd homologue) \(\xrightarrow{\text{add } \mathrm{-CH_2-}}\) \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3}\) (4th homologue) \(\xrightarrow{\text{add } \mathrm{-CH_2-}}\) \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3}\) (5th homologue).

By counting carbon and hydrogen atoms in the five homologues we get their molecular formulae as \(\mathrm{CH_4}\), \(\mathrm{C_2H_6}\), \(\mathrm{C_3H_8}\), \(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\) and \(\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}\). Comparing these molecular formulae, the following general formula is deduced : \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}\).

stem: Write down structural formulae of (a) the third higher and (b) the second lower homologue of \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH}\).
solution:
a. Structural formula of the third higher homologue is obtained by adding three \(\mathrm{-CH_2-}\) units to the carbon chain of the given structure.

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{add three } \mathrm{-CH_2-} \text{ units}} \mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-COOH}\) (third higher homologue)

b. Structural formula of the second lower homologue is obtained by removing two \(\mathrm{-CH_2-}\) units from the carbon chain of the given structure.

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{remove two } \mathrm{-CH_2-} \text{ units}} \mathrm{H-COOH}\)

| \(\mathrm{C(C_2H_5)_4}\) | | | |

Write IUPAC names for the following structures :

i. \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-C(=O)-CH_2-CH_3}\)

ii. \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(NH_2)-CH_2-COOH}\)

iii. \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_2-OH}\)

iv. \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH=CH_2}\)
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the question poses FOUR structures, i to iv, but the book's printed Solution stops after (ii) — the box closes on '3-aminobutanoic acid' and nothing on the following page continues it. Parts (iii) and (iv) below are worked here in the book's own style so the example answers everything it asks; parts (i) and (ii) are the book's own.]

i. \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-C(=O)-CH_2-CH_3}\)

Here the principal functional group, ketone is located at the C-3 on the five carbon chain. The -OH group, the hydroxyl substituent is at C-2. Therefore the IUPAC name is 2-hydroxypentan-3-one.

ii. \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(NH_2)-CH_2-COOH}\)

Here the principal functional group is carboxylic acid. The amino substituent is located at C-3 on four carbon chain. Therefore the IUPAC name 3-aminobutanoic acid.

iii. \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_2-OH}\)

Here the principal functional group is the alcohol, and there are two of them, so the suffix is -diol on a three carbon chain. Numbering from the \(\mathrm{-CH_2OH}\) end puts the two hydroxyl groups on C-1 and C-2, which is lower than the \(\{2, 3\}\) obtained by numbering the other way. Therefore the IUPAC name is propane-1,2-diol.

iv. \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH=CH_2}\)

Here there is no functional group other than the two carbon-carbon double bonds, on a four carbon chain. Two double bonds make the ending 'diene', and the 'a' of the alkane name is retained before it. Numbering from either end places the double bonds between C-1 and C-2 and between C-3 and C-4. Therefore the IUPAC name is buta-1,3-diene.

stem: Identify the nucleophile and electrophile from \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) and \(\mathrm{\overset{\oplus}{C}H_3}\). Also indicate the nucleophilic and electrophilic centres in them. Justify.
solution:
The structural formulae of two reagents showing all the valence electrons are :

\(\mathrm{H-\underset{H}{\overset{\bullet\bullet}{N}}-H}\) and \(\mathrm{H-\underset{H}{\overset{\oplus}{C}}-H}\)

Thus \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) contains N with a lone pair of electrons which can be given away to another species. Therefore \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) is a nucleophile and 'N' in it is the nucleophilic centre. The \(\mathrm{\overset{\oplus}{C}H_3}\) is a positively charged electron deficient species having a vacant orbital on the carbon. It is an electrophile. The 'C' in it is the electrophilic centre.

stem:
Consider the following molecules and answer the questions,

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-Cl}\), \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-Br}\), \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-I}\).

(i) What type of inductive effect is expected to operate in these molecules ?

(ii) Identify the molecules from these three, having the strongest and the weakest inductive effect.
solution:
(i) The groups responsible for inductive effect in these molecules are -Cl, -Br and -I, respectively. All these are halogen atoms which are more electronegative than carbon and therefore all of them exert - I effect, that is, electron withdrawing inductive effect.

(ii) The - I effect of halogens is due to their electronegativity. A decreasing order of electronegativity in these halogens follows Cl > Br > I. Therefore the strongest -I effect is expected in \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-Cl}\), while the weakest -I effect is expected for \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-I}\).

stem: Which of the \(\mathrm{CH_3-CHCl_2}\) and \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl}\) is expected to have stronger -I effect ?
solution: The group exerting -I effect in \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl}\) is one - Cl while in \(\mathrm{CH_3-CHCl_2}\) there are two - Cl atoms. Therefore \(\mathrm{CH_3-CHCl_2}\) is expected to have strong -I effect.

stem:
Identify the species that contains a conjugated system of \(\pi\) bonds. Explain your answer.

\(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2-CH=CH_2}\)  (I)

\(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH=CH-CH_3}\)  (II)
solution:
I Does not contain conjugated system of \(\pi\) bonds, as the two C = C double bonds are separated by two C - C single bonds.

II Contains a conjugated system of \(\pi\) bonds, as the two C = C double bonds are saparated by only one C - C single bond.

stem: Write resonance structures of \(\mathrm{H-COO^{\ominus}}\) and comment on their relative stability.
solution:
First the detailed bond structure of \(\mathrm{H-COO^{\ominus}}\) showing all the valence electron is drawn and then other resonance strucutres are generated using curved arrow to show movement of \(\pi\)-electrons. Two resonance structures are written for \(\mathrm{H-COO^{\ominus}}\).

\(\mathrm{H-C(=O)-O^{\ominus}}\) (I) \(\longleftrightarrow\) \(\mathrm{H-C(-O^{\ominus})=O}\) (II)

Both the resonance structures I and II are equivalent to each other, and therefore, are equally stable.

stem:
Identify the species which has resonance stabilization. Justify your answer.

(i) \(\mathrm{CH_3-\overset{\bullet\bullet}{O}-H}\)  (ii) \(\mathrm{CH_3-NO_2}\)  (iii) buta - 1, 3 - diene
solution:
(i) The bond structure shows that there is no \(\pi\) bond. Therefore no resonance and no resonance stabilization.

(ii) \(\mathrm{CH_3-\overset{\oplus}{N}(=O)-O^{\ominus}}\) \(\longleftrightarrow\) \(\mathrm{CH_3-\overset{\oplus}{N}(-O^{\ominus})=O}\)

N = O double bond is attached to 'O' which carries lone pair of electrons in a p orbital. Therefore resonance strucutres can be written and species is resonance stabilized.

(iii) \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH=CH_2}\) \(\longleftrightarrow\) \(\mathrm{\overset{\oplus}{C}H_2-CH=CH-\overset{\ominus}{C}H_2}\)

The Lewis structure shows two C=C double bonds alternating with a C-C single bond. Therefore resonance structures can be written as shown, and the species is resonance stabilized.

stem: Write three resonance structures for \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CHO}\). Indicate their relative stabilties and explain.
solution:
\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-C(=O)-H}\) (I) \(\longleftrightarrow\) \(\mathrm{CH_3-\overset{\oplus}{C}H-CH=C(H)-O^{\ominus}}\) (II) \(\longleftrightarrow\) \(\mathrm{CH_3-\overset{\ominus}{C}H-CH=C(H)-O^{\oplus}}\) (III)

Stabilty order : I > II > III

I : Contains more number of covalent bonds, each carbon atom and oxygen atom has complete octet, and involves no separation of opposite charges. Therefore the most stable resonance structure.

II : Contains one covalent bond less than in I, one carbon (\(\mathrm{C^{\oplus}}\)) has only 6 valence electrons, involves separation of opposite charges; the resonance structure II has -ve charge on more electronegative 'O' and +ve charge on more electroposoitve 'C'. It has intermediate stability.

III : Contains one covalent bond less than in I, oxygen has only 6 valence electrons, involves separation of opposite charge , has -ve charge on the more electropositive 'C' and +ve charge on more electronegative 'O'. All these factors are unfavourable for stability. Therefore it is the least stable.
